# Rule catalogue

Every rule `dpa-review` runs, generated from the rules in [`src/dpa_review/checks.py`](../src/dpa_review/checks.py). A finding is open when its status is `MISSING` or `NEEDS_REVIEW`. Any open `HIGH` finding makes the packet `BLOCKED` (exit `2`); any other open finding makes it `NEEDS_REVIEW` (exit `1`); otherwise it is `CLEARED_FOR_REVIEW` (exit `0`), which still needs a lawyer's sign-off. Input keys are described in [input-format.md](input-format.md).

## Transfer rules by basis

`transfer.<country>` checks each direct destination and `transfer.subprocessor.<name>` each sub-processor outside the EEA. Both use the same assessment of the country and the recorded mechanism (status and severity). The table shows each mechanism with nothing else recorded: for `dpf`, no certification on the Data Privacy Framework List; for `derogation_art49`, a transfer not recorded as occasional and not repetitive; for an Art. 46 safeguard, no transfer impact assessment. Art. 46(1) makes the safeguards the transfer basis only in the absence of an adequacy decision, so a safeguard recorded for a destination with a decision is not needed where the decision covers the importer. Where the decision has a scope limit the tool cannot check, the finding asks whether the importer is within it; once a transfer impact assessment is recorded that finding is LOW instead of MEDIUM. The United States has such a decision: Implementing Decision (EU) 2023/1795 covers only organisations on the Data Privacy Framework List, so a safeguard recorded for the US gets the same question, about that list.

## Reference data

The country lists the transfer rules use, as they stand in `checks.py`. Every adequacy decision below was read on EUR-Lex on 2026-11-10: its operative part, its date, its Official Journal reference and the EUR-Lex record of its status and amendments. The scope limit is the decision's own; the tool cannot check it from the input, so a finding that relies on the decision states it. Decisions are amended, extended and adopted after that date: re-check the decision on EUR-Lex before relying on a result.

Decisions adopted under Article 25(6) of Directive 95/46/EC stay in force under Art. 45(9) GDPR until amended, replaced or repealed; their findings cite Art. 45(9) too. Implementing Decision (EU) 2016/2295 replaced their articles on suspending data flows and on monitoring and left Article 1 unchanged. The US decision is reached through the `dpf` mechanism, with the importer's certification, so the US is not on the adequacy list. The tool models countries only: Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2025/1382 of 15 July 2025 on the European Patent Organisation, an international organisation, is not on the list.
